item.title: Pointed Gromov-Hausdorff Distance between $l^p$-Wedge Sums and Isometric Embeddings of $l^\infty$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paper studies $l^p$-wedge sums of metric spaces and provides a two-sided estimate for the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff distance between them. Using an upper bound for the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, the existence of an isometric embedding of $l^\infty$ into the Gromov-Hausdorff space of all non-empty metric spaces is proved.
item.dc:creator: Emin Abdullaev

item.title: Each simplex in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has a point with at least $14$ emanating normals to its boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.13475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that each simplex in $\mathbb{R}^4$ contains a point with at least $14$ emanating normals to the boundary. Earlier, the authors proved that each generic simple polytope in $\mathbb{R}^4$ contains a point with at least $12$ emanating normals to the boundary. This problem belongs to a piecewise linear counterpart of a longstanding problem concerning normals to smooth convex bodies.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Nasonov, Gaiane Panina

item.title: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
item.description: arXiv:2610.12619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a positive integer $d$, let $\Delta_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $\Delta_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.
item.dc:creator: Nihar Gargava, Matthias Gr\"obner, Michael Simkin

item.title: Cohomology and multiplicative gaps for quasi-isometries of nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct two word metrics on the same seven-dimensional torsion-free nilpotent lattice whose asymptotic cones are isometric, but for which every quasi-isometry has multiplicative constant at least $1+\varepsilon$, for one fixed $\varepsilon>0$. We use a convex invariant of a fixed quasi-isometry $\Psi:N\to M$. The displacement cocycle of $\Psi$ and the right-invariant means on $N$ determine a compact convex set $\mathcal A(\Psi)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V_N,V_M)$. If $\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi)$ denotes the first-layer maps of the graded homomorphisms that occur as blow-downs of $\Psi$ with varying basepoints, then $$ \mathcal A(\Psi)=\operatorname{conv}\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi), \qquad\operatorname{Ext}\mathcal A(\Psi)\subseteq\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(\Psi). $$ For every extreme point $L\in\mathcal A(\Psi)$, the dual map $L^*$ is also the degree-one part of an isomorphism of the full real cohomology rings. This cohomological compatibility, together with the realization of first-layer Pansu differentials by invariant means, yields the multiplicative constant gap stated above.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Soumyadeb Samanta, Soumyadip Thandar

item.title: Necessary conditions for benchmarking next-generation AI in materials discovery
item.description: arXiv:2610.13885v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current AI predicts materials by speeding up energy minimisation and training on large databases. However, scaling data generation prevents manual analysis by domain experts. If novelty is evaluated by chemical compositions or traditional representations in Crystallographic Information Files, or standard structure matchers based on manually chosen thresholds, one can easily generate millions of ``new'' compositions or files without discovering truly novel materials. This paper uses a hierarchy of crystal invariants to continuously trace and quantify structural novelty based on the new mathematical definition of a crystal structure and asymptotic guarantees for invariant descriptors. The invariant-based analysis through cascade computations on a modest computer exposes the unexpected scale of duplication in the world's largest materials databases, shown here in the high-profile case of GNoME datasets. To prevent current ``embarrassment of over-prediction'', we propose necessary conditions for next-generation AI that should be automatically enforced before claiming any new materials.
item.dc:creator: Daniel E Widdowson, Tatiana V Kurlina, Olga D Anosova, Vitaliy A Kurlin

item.title: The Canonical Induced Metric for Topological Branched Coverings and Geometric Applications
item.description: arXiv:1509.02638v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a continuous map $f:X\to Y$ from a continuum-connected space into a metric space, we introduce an associated canonical pullback metric $d_f$ on $X$ by combining the target diameter structure with the Mazurkiewicz construction as \[ d_f(x,x')=\inf\{\operatorname{diam}_Y f(E): E\subset X\text{ is a continuum containing }x,x'\}. \] Our main result shows that if $f:(X,\rho)\to Y$ is $L$-BDD, then $d_f$ is quantitatively equivalent to the Mazurkiewicz metric $\rho_M$, $(d_f)_M=d_f$, every continuum satisfies $\operatorname{diam}_{d_f}E=\operatorname{diam}_Y f(E)$ and $f:(X,d_f)\to Y$ is $1$-BDD and hence $1$-BLD. For bounded-turning spaces, this identifies a canonical bi-Lipschitz metric realization in the sense that every finite-to-one topological branched covering onto a locally length metric manifold admits such a compatible induced metric without any a priori BDD hypothesis. There are two main geometric applications of the induced pullback metric. Firstly, we prove an index-free quantitative porosity theorem for branch sets and their images at points of controlled linear or inverse linear dilatation, extending the well-known Bonk-Heinonen theorem and Sarvas theorem for branch set of Euclidean quasiregular mappings to a large class of metric spaces. Secondly, we prove that every finite-to-one BDD branched covering over a doubling bounded-turning target space admits a quantitative bi-Lipschitz embedding into the target times a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. As direct corollaries, we solve several well-known open problems asked by Heinonen, Rickman and Semmes.
item.dc:creator: Chang-Yu Guo, Marshall Williams

item.title: Limits of mapping packages and tangents of Sobolev maps
item.description: arXiv:2608.13124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show the existence of ultralimits of sequences of Hajlasz-Sobolev mappings $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ when $X_i$ converges to a limit space in the pointed measured Gromov (pmG) sense, partially extending recent results in [T. Ikonen and S. Wenger, (2026), arXiv:2603.05246]. We moreover demonstrate that the mappings pmG-converge to the ultralimit in a suitable sense, and obtain Arzela-Ascoli theorems in the context of pmG-convergence. As an application, we establish a version of Preiss's phenomenon for Hajlasz-Sobolev maps $f:(X,\mu)\to V$ into arbitrary Banach spaces. Besides extending it to maps into infinite dimensional targets, our result generalizes existing versions of Preiss's phenomenon [G. C. David, Geom. Funct. Anal., 25 (2015)], [N. Gigli, A. Mondino, and T. Rajala, J. Reine Angew. Math., 705 (2015)] by establishing it for pointed measured Gromov-Hausdorff tangents without a doubling assumption.
item.dc:creator: Milica Cakovi\'{c}, Elefterios Soultanis

item.title: Dual $L_p$ John ellipsoids for general measures
item.description: arXiv:2608.21958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dual $L_p$ John ellipsoids form a family that includes the origin-centered L\"owner and Legendre ellipsoids. In this paper, we extend this family to general measures within the dual weighted $L_p$ Brunn--Minkowski theory. For measures with locally integrable densities that are continuous in a neighborhood of the boundary of the given star body, we establish a variational formula for $L_p$-harmonic radial combinations. The associated boundary integral leads to an optimization problem that remains meaningful under weaker assumptions on the boundary trace of the density. We prove the existence, uniqueness, and characterization of its solution. The resulting ellipsoids include the dual $L_p$ John ellipsoids for Gaussian measures. We also establish a monotonicity inequality, a measure inequality for homogeneous densities with its equality conditions on the weighted support, and an $L_p$ L\"owner inclusion.
item.dc:creator: Ai-Jun Li, Baihe Liu, Qingzhong Huang

item.title: Chasing rotational symmetry in the spectre tiling
item.description: arXiv:2609.07592v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify the rotational symmetry centers in the spectre tiling. We find that both 2-fold and 3-fold symmetry centers are coexisting, with two different types of 3-fold centers. Local and global symmetry operations are distinguished, and characterized in terms of substitution systems. We introduce a decomposition of the spectre tiling in terms of three metatiles named diabolo, 2-arms and 3-arms, valid at any substitution level. We propose geometrical constructions for generating patches of the spectre tiling with 2-fold and 3-fold global rotational symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Marianne Imperor-Clerc, Jean-Francois Sadoc, Simon Tatham

item.title: Exact versus monotone isoperimetric profiles of finitely generated groups
item.description: arXiv:2509.22260v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gromov asked whether the exact isoperimetric profile of an infinite finitely generated group is comparable, at the same cardinality, to its greatest nondecreasing minorant. We compare finite sets with their translates and construct orders for which the first $r$ vertices have boundary bounded by a fixed multiple of that of the whole set. Such orders follow from profile summability or from rays in Schreier graphs with a uniform bound on the number using each edge. Among infinite finitely generated groups, we obtain comparison and nested exhaustions for elementary amenable and branch groups, direct products of at least two infinite groups, restricted wreath products with two nontrivial factors, and certain simple topological full groups, including amenable derived groups of interval exchanges. The exhausting $n$-point sets have boundary comparable to the monotone profile at $n$. The ray condition is quasi-isometry invariant and holds for the Sierpi\'nski-carpet group. For polycyclic groups of exponential growth, we refine Pittet's construction to obtain explicit nested sets with $|F_n|=n$ and $|\partial F_n|\asymp n/\log n$, answering his question with exact rather than comparable cardinalities. We also prove that the normalized $L^1$ profile satisfies $j(v)\le C(v/u)j(u)$ for $1\le u\le v$ on every infinite connected bounded-degree vertex-transitive graph. This yields the separation bound asked for by Gournay--Le Coz and Hume's Dirichlet--Neumann comparison at $p=1$. For groups of exponential growth, the exact-to-monotone comparison ratio is $O(\log\log n)$. We answer the first part of Correia's Question 1.3 positively by proving the required dilation regularity, and the second negatively by constructing elementary amenable examples whose inverse compositions fail this regularity for every choice of equivalent representatives.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee

item.title: Stable-norm boundary geometry on once-punctured tori
item.description: arXiv:2605.14574v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use normal-turn estimates to study the local and global geometry of the boundaries of stable-norm balls $B_X$ for complete finite-area hyperbolic once-punctured tori $X$. We show that the boundary $\partial B_X$ is a convex-geometric detector of exponential Diophantine approximation: rational directions give genuine corners with exponentially small exterior angles, while at an irrational direction $\beta$ the graph-flatness order admits an explicit formula in terms of the exponential rate at which rational directions approach $\beta$ and the $\ell^\infty$-radius of $B_X$ in the projective direction $\beta$. Thus irrational directions are not uniformly flat to infinite order, correcting the McShane--Rivin local picture. We also determine all possible irrational flatness orders and the size of the corresponding level sets. The computation of the rational corners unexpectedly yields a new McShane-type identity for the area of the dual body $B_X^*$: $$ \operatorname{Area}(B_X^*) = 4\sum_{\gamma} \ell_X(\gamma) \log\coth\left(\frac{\ell_X(\gamma)}{2}\right), $$ where the sum is over unoriented simple closed geodesics on $X$. As another global application, the normal-turn estimates also give a logarithmic-square bound for the number of integer points on the boundary of each dilated norm ball. Consequently, the number of simple closed geodesics of length exactly $L\geq2$ is at most $C_X(\log L)^2$. For the modular torus this yields $$ \#\lambda_M^{-1}(m)\leq C(\log\log(3m))^2 $$ for every Markoff number $m$, improving the previous logarithmic bounds for Markoff fibers.
item.dc:creator: Nhat Minh Doan, Xiaobin Li, Van Nguyen
